$comment: The exposure decision for dynamic-UI generation, and the response shapes that cannot be derived from the code. gen-data-manifest.mjs reads this and emits common/surface/data-manifest.json. TWO HALVES, for different reasons. `scopes` is the security boundary: a registered data function is NOT generatable until it is named here, so the default for anything new is closed. `sources` carries what the frontend cannot know about itself - every usage function is `return fetchApi(url)` with no type information, so the response shape is a claim about a backend in another service and has to be written down. Name, route, argsShape and callStyle are all DERIVED from usage-service.js and must not be written here; --check fails if they drift. The rule for adding a shape is the one the hand-written manifest set: it must be verified against a real consumer or a real backend handoff, not guessed from the endpoint name. `withheld` is where a registered function goes when it fails that test.

withheld.fetchSpendCalendar: Registered and routable, but no panel consumes it and no handoff documents its response, so there is no verified shape to declare. Exposing it would put a guessed shape in front of the model, which is how a dashboard binds to fields that do not exist. Add it the day a month-heatmap consumer or a backend doc pins the shape.
withheld.fetchFinopsAttributions: Same: the standalone sortable/paginated envelope is unverified. The attribution rows themselves ARE verified and are now reachable through fetchTokenopsDashboard's data.attributions.rows, which is the path tokenops-page.js itself prefers - so withholding this costs the model nothing today.

fetchTokenopsDashboard.description: Fleet-wide FinOps for a time window: a ten-metric KPI strip with server-computed deltas, per-agent rows, and a pre-computed top-5 spend split at data.spend_by_agent ready to feed a donut without any client-side aggregation. Real backend: GET /api/observability/finops/dashboard.
fetchTokenopsDashboard.$shapeSource: Read field-by-field off FinopsDashboardData and its structs in oss/server/src/observability/service.rs:787 (FinopsKpis:879, FinopsSummary:800, AgentFinopsRow:813, SpendByAgentBreakdown:980, SpendPieSlice, FinopsTokenUsage). The hand-written shape had drifted badly after 6987b124 and 3678327c: `spend_by_agent` was absent entirely, `kpis` was missing six of its ten metrics, `agents[]` was missing four, and — the one that actively misled — `token_usage` declared avg_latency_ms, container_hours and version, none of which the struct has. A model binding to a field that does not exist gets nothing and no diagnostic; the renderer can only check what the DSL says against the catalog, never against the response.

argHints.range: "24h" | "7d" | "30d" — wins over startTime/endTime when both are sent
argHints.view: "agent" | "workflow" — which shape attributions.rows comes back in
argHints.provider: string, optional — accepted but stubbed, no real filtering yet
argHints.orgUnit: string, optional — accepted but stubbed, no real filtering yet

fetchSpendTimeseries.description: Spend and operation counts bucketed over a time window - the series behind a spend-over-time chart. Each point also carries tool calls, that bucket's top-spending agent, and p50/p95/p99 latency. Real backend: GET /api/observability/finops/spend-timeseries.
fetchSpendTimeseries.$shapeSource: FinopsSpendTimeseries and SpendTimeseriesPoint, oss/server/src/observability/service.rs:896. Six of the point's nine fields were undeclared — tool_calls, top_agent_name, top_agent_spend_usd and the three latency percentiles.

fetchSpendCalendarDay.description: One calendar day's hourly spend curve, with each hour's own top-agent split, plus that day's average hourly spend and a pre-computed top-agents ranking. Real backend: GET /api/observability/finops/spend-calendar-day.
fetchSpendCalendarDay.$shapeSource: FinopsDayDrilldown, SpendHourPoint and AgentSpendSlice in oss/server/src/observability/service.rs. `date` was undeclared, and each hour carries its own top_agents/others_spend_usd that the old shape flattened away.

argHints.date: "YYYY-MM-DD", required — a calendar day, not a range

fetchUsageSummary.description: The CALLER'S OWN usage summary over a fixed 30-day window — not the fleet's (oss/server/src/usage/routes.rs:68). No arguments. For fleet totals use fetchTokenopsDashboard's data.summary. Real backend: GET /usage/summary.

fetchUsageHistory.description: The CALLER'S OWN usage per day over the last N days — not the fleet's (oss/server/src/usage/routes.rs:131). For a fleet spend series use fetchSpendTimeseries. Real backend: GET /usage/history?days=N.

fetchUsageByAgent.description: The CALLER'S OWN usage, grouped by agent — not the fleet's. The SQL filters on the session user (oss/server/src/usage/routes.rs:256) and looks back a fixed 30 days (routes.rs:243, default_days at routes.rs:32; the frontend never sends `days`, so no range filter reaches it). On a deployment where the agents run under other identities this returns zero rows while the fleet dashboard is full, which reads as a broken table. For a FLEET-WIDE per-agent table use fetchTokenopsDashboard's data.attributions.rows instead. Real backend: GET /usage/by-agent.

fetchUsageByModel.description: The CALLER'S OWN usage, grouped by provider/model — not the fleet's. Same caller filter and same fixed 30-day window as fetchUsageByAgent (oss/server/src/usage/routes.rs). There is no fleet-wide by-model source in scope today; do not present this as one. Real backend: GET /usage/by-model.

$comment2: `answers` is what KIND of question each source settles — summary, series, breakdown, composite — and it is the half the manifest never said. Every line used to read as a way to fetch tokenops data, so a request for a comprehensive dashboard went to whichever description sounded most complete, and the model then drew the one row set it had in hand twice. Chart shapes follow data shapes; this is what makes the data shapes visible. gen-data-manifest.mjs checks each claim against the declared responseShape, so a source cannot say `series` without a time field in it.
